family.description: This Domain of unknown function 61 (DUF61) family of proteins are widely distributed in archaea. In crenarchaea, the genes of DUF61 proteins are in an operon containing two genes of box C/D RNA protein complexes. The NMR structure of a DUF61 family member from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Sulfolobus solfataricus revealed a rigid core structure and flexible N- and C-terminal regions, including a negatively-charged independent C-terminal helix. The core structure consists of N- and C-terminal subdomains, in which the C-terminal subdomain shows significant structural similarity with several nucleic acid binding proteins [[cite:PUB00098020]].

evidence.explanation: Zhou2018 abstract and PDB5VFK metadata support structural observations for SSO0941. The full paper and supplements were not inspected. Twenty submitted NMR conformers are not twenty biological replicates; the author-defined monomer assignment is not an activity requirement. InterPro and RCSB repetition of this abstract is one evidential origin.

Wang2024 selected Results and simulation Methods plus original Figure2 place SSO0941 in an energy/force benchmark. Fragmented-DFT comparison and computational samples are not DUF61 biological perturbation data. No RNA-processing edge is supported by the inspected benchmark sections.

discussions.notes: No causal edge is supported by the inspected material; this is not an exhaustive absence claim. The current 196-entry UniProt query returned no FUNCTION comments, which is annotation coverage rather than proof that no functional experiments exist. Full-paper and member-specific functional follow-up remain open. Minimal assessments and access/search limits are retained under evidence/PF01886. No dummy graph is added.
discussions.prompt: Obtain a verified DUF61 member-specific perturbation or substrate assay before adding a causal graph.
discussions.rationale: The inspected SSO0941 structural abstract, deposition and later computational benchmark do not establish a directed biological effect. Box C/D RNA operon proximity and nucleic-acid-binding fold similarities motivate research but do not demonstrate RNA binding, processing or a DUF61-dependent cellular pathway.

evidence.explanation: Current member-specific InterPro maps Q97ZH2 to PF01886 at 4-123. UniProt sequence version1, entry version93, identifies Saccharolobus solfataricus P2, taxon273057; AAK41217.1 and WP_009992374.1 match the reference exactly. Historical Sulfolobus naming is retained as an alias, not a separate tested species.

PDB5VFK entity1 is exactly the 138-residue reference plus the eight-residue LEHHHHHH suffix. Its one protein entity and lack of an RNA/DNA polymer entity do not test all possible ligands. The deposited pH4.4 and310K describe the NMR sample, not a functional optimum.

discussions.notes: UPF0216 is a verified family alias through O29789/AF_0460 with PF01886 and IPR002746, not functional characterization. ScienceDirect access returned403 and Elsevier API supplied metadata only; the CAS entry links the DOI without full text. BMRB30279 access was unresolved, not proof of data withdrawal. All196 frozen proteins require member-specific assessment before family-wide transfer.
discussions.prompt: Preserve SSO0941 reference, Pfam interval and tagged-construct scope when evaluating functional evidence.
discussions.rationale: A protein structure is not an isolated-domain functional test. Q97ZH2 has 138 residues, PF01886 covers 4-123 inclusive, and PDB5VFK entity1 contains the complete reference plus LEHHHHHH. Any future whole-protein phenotype must not silently become a domain- or residue-specific mechanism.
